guard.notes: OpenCode has no declarative hooks key in opencode.json, so the adapter is a project plugin: .opencode/plugins/agentos-guard.ts subscribes to tool.execute.before, pipes {tool_name, tool_input} to .agents/runtime/guard.mjs with AGENT_RUNTIME=opencode and AGENT_RUNTIME_CONFIG=.agents/runtime/opencode/config.json, and throws on exit 2 - a thrown error denies the tool call, so the policy is enforced by the harness. warn-level hits go to the OpenCode log via client.app.log. The plugin runs under Bun; guard.mjs is spawned with node.

capabilitiesNotes: OpenCode was added to this repository on 2026-09-30 together with its adapter; nothing here has exercised a session yet, so every capability is unknown rather than assumed. toolEvents: the plugin can observe every tool call through tool.execute.before/after, but no event has been recorded in this repository yet - it moves to verified at first exercised run. The plugin API also exposes session.*, permission.* and message.* events, which is the surface the console emitter would use.
pricingNotes: OpenCode is bring-your-own-provider: models resolve against the providers configured for the user (auth), not against this file. The tiers above are the intended mapping; confirm them with the user at first launch, write the confirmed values back and flip verified per tier. No rates are recorded; `delivery estimate --runtime opencode` warns and falls back to the placeholder table.

permissions.notes: Reads and writes go through OpenCode's own permission prompts; the plugin guard adds this repository's policy on top (throw denies the call). Structural changes to roles, agents or skills always need explicit user approval, in every mode.
